lines.japanese: 「ごご、ごめっ──」
lines.english: “S-s-sorr—”

lines.japanese: 「うんおはよう」
lines.english: “Morning.”

lines.japanese: 「──おおおはようなさい」
lines.english: “—g-g-good morningen.”

lines.japanese: ああ、謝ってる途中だったのか。割りこんじゃって悪いことをした。
lines.english: Oh. She'd been in the middle of apologizing. I felt bad for interrupting.

lines.japanese: 「で、なにがゴメンって？」
lines.english: “What were you sorry for?”

lines.japanese: 「えへへ、けさは目ざまし時計を手のとどく位置においちゃった」
lines.english: “Hee hee. I left the alarm clock where I could reach it this morning.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、寝過ごしちゃったと？」
lines.english: “Ah. So you overslept?”

lines.japanese: 「己に克つことは難しい」
lines.english: “Victory over oneself is difficult.”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、気にするな小鳩！　こうして俺を起こしに来てくれたんだ、おまえが謝る必要なんかないぞっ」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha! Don't worry about it, Kobato! You still came to wake me. You have nothing to apologize for!”

lines.japanese: 「だいたいおまえの優しいお兄ちゃんは、そんなつまらないことで怒るような心の狭い男じゃないからな。さあ、兄妹なかよく朝ごはんを食べて──」
lines.english: “Besides, your kind big brother isn't so small-minded that he'd get angry over something so trivial. Come, let us enjoy breakfast together in sibling harmony—”

lines.japanese: 「朝ごはん作る時間なくなっちゃった、たはは」
lines.english: “I ran out of time to make breakfast. Ta-ha-ha.”

lines.japanese: 「──ふざッけるなウヴァアアアア！」
lines.english: “—don't fuck with me! UVAAAAAAH!”

lines.japanese: 飢えに対する衝動的な恐怖が、俺の中のケモノを解放した。
lines.english: An instinctive terror of starvation released the beast inside me.

lines.japanese: 「ごはんはあるんだけど、簡単に作れるおかずがなくって。昨日の残りものもないんだあ」
lines.english: “There's rice, but nothing I can turn into a quick side dish. We don't have any leftovers from last night either.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、なーんだ、ライスはあるのか」
lines.english: “Oh. So we have rice.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩の無邪気な表情があまりに可愛かったので、気付けば奈落生まれのケモノも引きさがっていた。
lines.english: Kobato's innocent expression was so adorable that, before I knew it, even the beast born in the Abyss had withdrawn.

lines.japanese: 「うん、いいよいいよ。じゃあ今日はライスだけでいいよ」
lines.english: “That's fine, then. I'll just have rice today.”

lines.japanese: 「意味がわからない」
lines.english: “That makes no sense.”

lines.japanese: フードコーディネイター小鳩にとって、白米ウィズアウトおかずは理解しえぬ概念か。もはや麺のないかけそば的存在なのかな。
lines.english: To Food Coordinator Kobato, was white rice *without* a side dish an incomprehensible concept? Perhaps it was like a bowl of noodle soup with no noodles in it.

lines.japanese: 「いや、たまにはいいもんだよ？　ね、塩でもかけて食べよう。俺けっこう好きだよ塩ごはん」
lines.english: “It's all right once in a while. We can sprinkle salt on it. I quite like rice with salt.”

lines.japanese: 「なに言ってんの」
lines.english: “What are you talking about?”

lines.japanese: それすら許容範囲外か。小鳩なりに台所を任されてるプライドみたいのがあるのかな。スープの出来に納得できない日は店を開けない、頑固職人のラーメン屋みたいだ。
lines.english: Even that was beyond the pale. Perhaps she took a certain professional pride in running the kitchen, like some stubborn noodle-shop master who refused to open whenever the broth fell short of perfection.

lines.japanese: しかしそうは言っても、今からまともなおかずを作る時間は──
lines.english: But even so, there was no longer time to prepare a proper side dish—

lines.japanese: ──俺が時計を見ると小鳩も察したらしい。ちょっと申しわけなさそうに俯いてしまった。もちろん伏し目がちな小鳩も可愛いが、笑顔の小鳩はもっと可愛いのでなんとか安心させてあげたい。
lines.english: When I looked at the clock, Kobato seemed to understand. She lowered her head, looking a little guilty. Downcast Kobato was adorable too, of course, but smiling Kobato was even more adorable. I had to reassure her somehow.

lines.japanese: 「そうだなあ、それでは玉子かけごはんなんてどうだい？」
lines.english: “Let's see. How would egg over rice sound?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、醤油をかければアリかもしれない」
lines.english: “Hmm. It might work with soy sauce.”

lines.japanese: お、ちょっと前向きな反応。塩はナシでも玉子はアリなのか。ようし、もう少しで可愛い小鳩にまた会えるぞ！
lines.english: Oh, that was a little more positive. Salt was out, but egg was okay. Good! Just a little more and I'd see my adorable Kobato again!

lines.japanese: 「でもいま玉子も切れてる」
lines.english: “But we're out of eggs.”

lines.japanese: 「駄目じゃん」
lines.english: “Then it won't work.”

lines.japanese: ツイてないときはどこまでもツイてないもんだ。
lines.english: When luck turned against you, it kept going to the bitter end.

lines.japanese: 「あ、じゃあ、お隣りさんにもらってくる。玉子なら分けてもらえるかも」
lines.english: “Oh! Then I'll ask next door. Maybe they can spare an egg.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなのか」
lines.english: “Will they?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。となりのおばさん親切だから」
lines.english: “Mm. The lady next door is kind.”

lines.japanese: 親切……だったか？　俺的には、挨拶しても煮えきらない返事しかよこさない、愛想の悪いおばちゃんって印象しかないけど。
lines.english: Kind...? Was she? My only impression was of an unfriendly woman who gave vague, grudging answers even when greeted.

lines.japanese: 小鳩がぱたぱたと出ていった。引っ込み思案で人見知りする子だけど、ちゃんと甘えられるのかな。
lines.english: Kobato pattered out. She was shy and withdrawn around strangers. Would she manage to impose on the neighbor properly?

lines.japanese: ま、ご近所には良い子としてその名を轟かせてるらしい（叔母さん談）から大丈夫か。俺はしばらくテレビを見ながら小鳩の帰りを待った。
lines.english: Well, according to Auntie, her fame as a good girl thundered throughout the neighborhood. She would be fine. I watched television while I waited for her to return.

lines.japanese: あらどうしたのー、まあそれはたいへんねえー。
lines.english: Oh, what's the matter? My, that's terrible.

lines.japanese: あらあらまー、やだわー、あらーいいのよーたいへんねー、あらー。
lines.english: Oh my, oh goodness, nooo! Ohhh, it's fine, really. You poor thing. Oh myyy.

lines.japanese: いいのよー、それならもっていきなさいー、いいえこまったときはおたがいさまよー。
lines.english: It's fiiine, then take it with yooou. No, nooo, neighbors help each other in times of neeeed.

lines.japanese: ただいまー、ばたん。
lines.english: I'm hooome. Slam.

lines.japanese: 「やったっ！　おとなりさんにおかずと飲みものまで分けてもらっちゃった！」
lines.english: “Yes! The lady next door gave me side dishes and drinks too!”

lines.japanese: 「おおっ！」
lines.english: “Oh!”

lines.japanese: 帰ってきた小鳩の頭上には、いろいろ入ってるボウルが掲げられていた。どうやら保護欲くすぐりまくりな彼女の挙動は、無愛想な主婦さえも慈愛の女神へ豹変させてしまうらしい。
lines.english: Kobato came back holding a bowl of assorted things above her head. Everything she did seemed to tug so hard at people's protective instincts that even an unfriendly housewife had turned into a goddess of mercy.

lines.japanese: むぅ、俺の妹の可愛さが理解できるとは、なかなか見所のあるご婦人だ。今度うちにお歳暮が送られてきたときは、いかにも持てあましそうなインスタントコーヒーでもお裾分けしてあげよう。
lines.english: Hmm. A discerning woman, to recognize my sister's charms. The next time our family received year-end gifts, I would share some of the instant coffee we were obviously never going to finish.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ私、準備するから、お兄ちゃんも好きなだけごはんよそって」
lines.english: “I'll get everything ready, so serve yourself as much rice as you want.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は卓上に皿を並べたあと、お隣りさんからもらった惣菜をてきぱきと均等に分けていった。
lines.english: After setting out the plates, Kobato briskly divided the side dishes from next door into equal portions.

lines.japanese: 「あ、お兄ちゃんはブロッコリーいる？　いっぱい入れておくね」
lines.english: “Oh, big bro, do you want broccoli? I’ll give you lots.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、食べるぞ。ありがとう、モリモリ入れてくれ」
lines.english: “Yes, I do. Thank you. Pile it high.”

lines.japanese: 優しい妹だなあ。俺がブロッコリー＆マヨネーズの丸ごとサラダを好きだと知ってて、うううっ……。
lines.english: What a kind sister. She knew I loved a whole broccoli-and-mayonnaise salad. Ngh...

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃんニンジンは？」
lines.english: “What about carrots, big bro?”

lines.japanese: 「わりあい食べる」
lines.english: “I eat them reasonably often.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、いっぱい入れておくね！　玉ねぎは？」
lines.english: “Okay. I'll give you lots! What about onions?”

lines.japanese: 「適度に食べる」
lines.english: “In moderation.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、いっぱい入れておくね！」
lines.english: “Okay. I'll give you lots!”

lines.japanese: 「え、いや適度でいいんだけど……」
lines.english: “No, I said moderation was fine...”

lines.japanese: 「あ、キュウリとピーマンと黒いコーヒーはお兄ちゃんにあげるね。ううん、違うよ思いやりだよ？　やったね！」
lines.english: “Oh, you can have the cucumber, green pepper, and black coffee. No, you've got it all wrong. This is me being considerate, okay? Lucky you!”

lines.japanese: 「待てコラ」
lines.english: “Hold it right there.”

lines.japanese: 優しいと思っていた妹は、ただ自分の好みで選り分けていただけだった。
lines.english: The sister I had taken for kind had simply been sorting the food according to her own tastes.

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　てめ、なに自分の嫌いなモンだけ避けてんだよコノヤロウ、子供かおまえは」
lines.english: “Huh? Why are you picking out everything you hate and dumping it on me, asshole? What are you, a child?”

lines.japanese: 「うんっ」
lines.english: “Mm!”

lines.japanese: 「デスヨネー！」
lines.english: “WELL, YEAH!”

lines.japanese: ああもう、屈託のない笑顔が可愛いなあ。
lines.english: Oh, that carefree smile was adorable.

lines.japanese: もちろんその神々しいばかりの可愛さには抗いようもないので、俺は濃緑色野菜たっぷり朝定食（ブラックコーヒー付き）を笑顔でたいらげた。やったね！
lines.english: Naturally, her almost divine adorableness was impossible to resist. Smiling, I finished my dark-green-vegetable breakfast set, black coffee included. Lucky me!

lines.japanese: 「お、蛎崎うに売れてるんだ。『恋のサインカーブ』五週連続チャート入りだって」
lines.english: “Oh, Uni Kakizaki is doing well. ‘Love’s Sine Curve’ has charted five weeks running.”

lines.japanese: 朝食後。台所で食器類を洗ってくれている小鳩に届くよう、大きめの声で言った。
lines.english: After breakfast, I spoke loudly enough to reach Kobato as she washed the dishes in the kitchen.

lines.japanese: 「へー。お兄ちゃん、うにうに好き？」
lines.english: “Oh. Big bro, do you like Uni-Uni?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、なんか小鳩が好きみたいだから、俺も興味あるふりをしようと思って」
lines.english: “No. You seem to like her, so I thought I'd pretend to be interested too.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん？」
lines.english: “Hmm?”

lines.japanese: 「明日は知ったかぶって小鳩とアルバムの話もしてみようかな。たぶん何曲目のコード進行が～とか、何コーラス目のフレーズが～みたいな曖昧トークでボンヤリさせとけば、結構それっぽく騙せとおせると思うんだ」
lines.english: “Maybe tomorrow I'll bluff my way through a conversation with you about the album. If I keep it vague—‘the chord progression in track three’ or ‘that phrase in the second chorus’—I can probably keep the haze thick enough to fool you.”

lines.japanese: 朝の情報番組がお送りする邦楽ヒットチャート特集。とくべつ気になるわけでもなかったけど、なんとなく垂れ流しにしていた。
lines.english: The morning news show was running a feature on the Japanese pop charts. I wasn't especially interested, but I left it playing in the background.

lines.japanese: 「おおすげえ。大津波ザザブロウ、演歌なのにトップ１０入りしてる」
lines.english: “Oh, impressive. Otsunami Zazaburo made the top ten with a traditional ballad.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩の返事はない。演歌には興味がないみたいだ。
lines.english: Kobato did not answer. Traditional ballads apparently held no interest for her.

lines.japanese: 「あ、御影クリヤの『Ｎｅｏｎ　Ｓｉｇｎ』だ。これもいま売れてるよなあ」
lines.english: “Oh, it's Kuriya Mikage's 'Neon Sign.' This one's selling well too.”

lines.japanese: やっぱり返事がない。洗い物に集中してるみたいだ。
lines.english: Still no answer. She seemed focused on doing the dishes.

lines.japanese: 番組はシングルチャートを終えて、アルバムチャートへと移っていた。
lines.english: The program finished the singles chart and moved on to albums.

lines.japanese: 「あっ！」
lines.english: “Ah!”

lines.japanese: 今週の第９位、地味ながらミドル世代の支持を受けてのロングセール、との前置きを受けて紹介されたのは、フリッキー５のベストアルバム『ロシアン妊娠検査薬』復刻盤。
lines.english: This week's number nine—introduced as an unobtrusive long seller sustained by the middle-aged market—was the reissue of Fricky Five's best-of album *Russian Pregnancy Test*.

lines.japanese: 「いやっほう！　素晴らしい！　さァ～っすがフリッキー５、時空を超えたぼくらのカリスマっすよ！」
lines.english: “Yee-haw! Magnificent! That's Fricky Five for you—our idols transcending space and time!”

lines.japanese: 俺の中の５分の１が勝手に盛りあがっていた。
lines.english: One-fifth of me had become excited without permission.

lines.japanese: 「え、どうしたの」
lines.english: “Huh? What's wrong?”

lines.japanese: 誰も聞いてないのに暑苦しく騒いでいた甲斐あって、気付いたら小鳩がふきんで手を拭き拭き、後ろに立っていた。
lines.english: All that overheated shouting to nobody had paid off. When I noticed, Kobato stood behind me, drying her hands on a dishcloth.

lines.japanese: ううっ、こんなめんどくさいお兄ちゃんの相手をしてくれるなんていい子だなあ。
lines.english: Ngh, what a good kid, putting up with such a pain-in-the-neck big brother.

lines.japanese: 「というわけで、お礼にフリッキー５のＣＤを貸してあげよう」
lines.english: “And so, as my thanks, I shall lend you a Fricky Five CD.”

lines.japanese: 「うええっ！？　い、いいよ！　いらない、いらないっ！」
lines.english: “What!? N-no! That's okay! I don't want it!”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、遠慮することなんかないぞ！　おっと、いまコンポが壊れてるなんていうイチゴくさい逃げは通用しないからな」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha! No need to be shy. And let me warn you: that strawberry-scented excuse about your stereo being broken won't work this time.”

lines.japanese: 「コンポはあるけど聴かないよ。捨てちゃいなよそんなの」
lines.english: “My stereo works. I'm still not listening to that. Throw it away.”

lines.japanese: 「自分ばかりか俺まで聞くなと！？」
lines.english: “You forbid not only yourself but even *me* to listen!?”

lines.japanese: 「記憶から抹消しちゃえばいいよ」
lines.english: “Erase it from your memory.”

lines.japanese: 「さながら親の仇のように！」
lines.english: “As if they had murdered your parents!”

lines.japanese: ああ、黙りこんじゃった。まったく米田優といい望月紀奈子といい、みんなしてフリファを終わってる扱いしちゃってさ。ええまあ、終わってるんですけど。
lines.english: Ah. She had fallen silent. Yu Yoneda, Kinako Mochizuki—everyone treated the Frickies as though the band were finished. Which, yes, they were.

lines.japanese: 「……うん分かった……やっぱり聴いてみるから貸して」
lines.english: “...Okay. I understand... I'll listen, so lend it to me.”
“What!?”

lines.japanese: しょぼくれる兄の姿を哀れと思ったのか、小鳩はゆっくり右手を差しだしてくれた。ううっ、なんて優しい子なんだ。
lines.english: Maybe she felt sorry for her dejected big brother, because Kobato slowly held out her right hand. Ngh, what a sweet kid.

lines.japanese: 「あ、でもそんなこと言って？　ははは、まさか部屋に戻ったら、こっそりゴミ箱にポイするつもりじゃないだろうな」
lines.english: “But are you sure? Ha ha ha. You're not planning to sneak back to your room and toss it in the garbage, are you?”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、ちゃんと分別して捨てる」
lines.english: “No. I'll dispose of it properly with the recycling.”

lines.japanese: 「地球に優しく兄には厳しい！」
lines.english: “Kind to the Earth, cruel to your brother!”

lines.japanese: あわわわわ……助けてくれえ、助けてくれえ。俺は大事な宝物を胸に抱きしめ二階へ逃げた。
lines.english: Oh no... Somebody save me! Save me! Clutching my precious treasure to my chest, I fled upstairs.

lines.japanese: でも小鳩はきっと、俺と同じく優れた感性を持っているはず。聴きさえすればフリファの良さを分かってくれるに違いない。そう、それだ。
lines.english: But surely Kobato possessed the same refined sensibilities as I. If only she listened, she was bound to understand what was so great about the Frickies. Yes. That was it.

lines.japanese: 俺は妹の部屋へ侵入すると（ていうかフツーにふすま開きっぱだった）、ＣＤをコンポにセットしたのち、取りだせないよう幾重にもガムテープでぐるぐる巻きにしておいた。やったね！
lines.english: I invaded my sister's room—the sliding door was simply standing wide open—put the CD in her stereo, then wound layer after layer of duct tape around the unit so she could not remove it. Lucky me!

lines.japanese: しかしすぐ見つかって小鳩に怒られた。
lines.english: She found it immediately and got angry.

lines.japanese: そんなわけで、通学コースは途中（柳木原駅の改札出たトコ）まで一緒だから兄妹仲良く登校しようと誘ったけど、ぷんすか小鳩にきっぱり断られてしまった。
lines.english: Our routes to school were the same until just beyond the ticket gates at Yanagihara Station, so I suggested we go together like good siblings. Still fuming, Kobato flatly refused.

lines.japanese: 俺はとてもしょんぼりしてしまった。しかし怒った小鳩もそれはそれで可愛かったため、テンション的にはプラマイ０となった。
lines.english: I was terribly dejected. But Kobato was adorable even when she was angry, so my mood came out at plus or minus zero.

lines.japanese: そして空想の中では小鳩がいっぱい俺に微笑んでくれたので、その後ぐんぐんプラスへ傾いていった。
lines.english: Then Kobato smiled at me over and over in my imagination, sending the total climbing steadily into positive territory.

lines.japanese: いやあ、兄妹って本当にいいものですね！
lines.english: Ah, siblings. Aren't they wonderful?

lines.japanese: 緩やかな傾斜を上がっていくと、赤いキャンバス屋根のたばこ屋が見えてきた。
lines.english: As I climbed the gentle slope, the tobacco shop's red canvas awning came into view.

lines.japanese: ふむ、どうしよう。看板娘の山科京は、今日も具合がよろしくないのだろうか。
lines.english: Hmm. What should I do? Was Miyako Yamashina, poster girl of the shop, feeling poorly again today?

lines.japanese: 俺のテンション的には、５０メートルほど助走を付けた渾身のフライングボディプレスおはようを送りたいところだが、彼女が昨日のような有様だったら致死行為になりかねない。
lines.english: At my present level of excitement, I wanted to take a fifty-meter running start and deliver a full-force flying-body-press good morning. But if she was in yesterday's condition, that might prove fatal.

lines.japanese: うーん……ま、無視するのも俺の美学に反するし、とりあえず一言だけ軽く挨拶して通りすぎていくか。
lines.english: Hmm... Still, ignoring her violated my aesthetic. I would offer one light greeting and continue on.

lines.japanese: そんな感じで方針を固めたのだが。
lines.english: That was the plan, but—

lines.japanese: 「おはよう」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 「おっ？　ああ、おはよう山科さん。今日は具合よさそうじゃない」
lines.english: “Oh? Ah, good morning, Yamashina. You seem better today.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、比較的ね」
lines.english: “Mm. Comparatively.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか。それはよかったね」
lines.english: “I see. That's good.”

lines.japanese: 「え、そう？　なんで？」
lines.english: “Is it? Why?”

lines.japanese: 「は？　なんでって……すまん、質問の意味が分からん」
lines.english: “Huh? Why...? Sorry, I don't understand the question.”

lines.japanese: 「私の体調がいいと……どうして羽田君が『よかったね』？」
lines.english: “If I'm feeling better... why is that ‘good’ for you, Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そりゃだってアレだろう。体調なんて、悪いよりは良い方がいいに決まってるだろう」
lines.english: “Well, obviously... Feeling well is better than feeling ill.”

lines.japanese: 「でも羽田君には関係なくない？」
lines.english: “But it doesn't have anything to do with you.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことはないぞ。クラスメイトの体調が悪かったら、そりゃ誰だって心配になるじゃないか」
lines.english: “Of course it does. If a classmate feels sick, anybody would worry.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで？」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese: ああ、ここで「なんで？」になるわけか。ずいぶん端折ったなあ。しかし──
lines.english: Ah, so she skipped straight to *why*. She had omitted rather a lot of steps. Still—

lines.japanese: 「──なんでじゃない！　おいおい何を言ってるんだ、君は。友達が辛ければ心配するだろうフツー。少なくとも俺の中の五分の一は、山科さんを全力で心配しているぞ！」
lines.english: “—there is no why! Come now, what are you saying? When your friend is suffering, you worry. That's normal. At least one-fifth of me is worrying about you with all its strength!”

lines.japanese: 「五分の一？」
lines.english: “One-fifth?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あー、いやまあ、そんなカンジだ」
lines.english: “Ah—well. Something like that.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふっ、カンジ悪いね」
lines.english: “Hee hee. That feels kind of mean.”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　ああ、たしかに失言なカンジだったな。ごめんなさいなカンジだ」
lines.english: “Hmm? Yeah, I guess that was kind of tactless. I'm kind of sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、いいよ。言われてみれば五分の一ってカンジするもん」
lines.english: “No, it's fine. Now that you mention it, you do feel about one-fifth familiar.”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、どんなだ、五分の一のカンジって」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha! What does one-fifth feel like?”

lines.japanese: 「私の知ってる羽田君が五分の一くらい」
lines.english: “About one-fifth of you is the Haneda I know.”

lines.japanese: 山科京、か……いい勘してるな。ちょっとフシギ入ってる感はあるが、ただのピンボケ娘ではなさそうだ。
lines.english: Miyako Yamashina... Her intuition was sharp. There was something faintly otherworldly about her, but she was no mere space case.

lines.japanese: しかし渡来明日香のように詮索したり、針生蔵人のように好奇の目を向けたりはして来ないようだ。ひとまず危険度はランク外としておこう。
lines.english: Yet she did not pry like Asuka Watarai or study me with Kurodo Hariu's curiosity. For now, I would leave her outside the threat rankings.

lines.japanese: 「ところで山科さん、学校には行かないのか」
lines.english: “By the way, Yamashina, aren't you going to school?”

lines.japanese: 「病状が良ければ行くよ？　今日はちょっと駄目そうだけど……」
lines.english: “I go when my condition allows. Today doesn't seem promising, though...”

lines.japanese: 「そうか、大変だな。でも良かったじゃないか、昨日よりは元気そうだ」
lines.english: “I see. That must be difficult. Still, this is good, isn't it? You seem healthier than yesterday.”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君のお陰だよ、ありがとう」
lines.english: “It's thanks to you, Haneda. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「俺の？　え、なんで……？」
lines.english: “Thanks to me? Why...?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだ」
lines.english: “Oh, right.”

lines.japanese: 山科京は俺の質問を無視して言った。
lines.english: Miyako Yamashina ignored my question.

lines.japanese: 「きのう卒業文集の制作作業をするって言ってたっけ？」
lines.english: “Did you say yesterday that we had to work on the graduation anthology?”

lines.japanese: 「え……ああ、そうだ、それ」
lines.english: “What...? Ah, yes. That.”

lines.japanese: 「要は、学校に来られるようになったら、山科さんにも参加して欲しいんだ。もちろん無理のない範囲で構わないんだけど……」
lines.english: “The point is, once you're well enough to come to school, I'd like you to participate too. Only as much as your health permits, of course...”

lines.japanese: 「うん、いいよ」
lines.english: “Sure.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか残念だが病気じゃ仕方な……えっ、いいの？」
lines.english: “I see. A shame, but if you’re ill, there’s nothing to—wait, you will?”

lines.japanese: 「月曜日に体が動いたらね」
lines.english: “If my body works on Monday.”

lines.japanese: こ、怖いことさらりと言うやつだな……。
lines.english: What a frightening thing to say so casually...

lines.japanese: でも本当に山科京が参加してくれれば、ようやっとまともな活動が出来るようになるだろう。
lines.english: But if Miyako Yamashina really joined us, we'd finally be able to get some proper work done.

lines.japanese: 面倒くせえなと愚痴る俺がいたけど、学園生活にハリが出てきたと燃える俺もいた。
lines.english: One part of me complained that it sounded like a pain. Another burned with excitement at the new purpose in our school life.

lines.japanese: その日の放課後。
lines.english: After school that day.

lines.japanese: 「ぱね田くぅ～ん」
lines.english: “Paneeedaaa.”

lines.japanese: 白々しいシュガーボイスで俺を呼ぶのは、例によって懲りないプリンセス渡来明日香だった。
lines.english: That sugary, obviously fake voice calling my name belonged, as always, to Princess Asuka Watarai, who never learned.

lines.japanese: 「なんだい、渡らないさん」
lines.english: “What is it, Miss Wata-don't?”

lines.japanese: 「なにソレ、そんな名前で呼んでいいって許可した覚えない」
lines.english: “What's that? I don't remember giving you permission to call me by a name like that.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は俺のすぐ前の椅子を、くるんと逆向きにして腰を下ろした。おいおい、そこおまえの席じゃないだろう、誰が座っていいと言ったんだ。
lines.english: She spun the chair right in front of me around and sat down facing me. Hey, that's not your seat. Who said you could sit there?

lines.japanese: 「まったく、ひとのことは変な名前で呼ぶくせに……じゃあ何ならいいんだ。渡ればいいのか。渡り蟹さんでどうだ」
lines.english: “Honestly. You call *me* strange names... Then what would satisfy you? Does it merely have to cross? How about Miss Migratory Crab?”

lines.japanese: 「せめて渡り鳥とかにしようよ。あ、渡り鳥明日香ってカッチョよくない？　どう？」
lines.english: “At least make it a migratory bird. Oh! Doesn't Asuka the Migratory Bird sound cool? What do you think?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、でもね渡る世間は鬼ばかりさん、ネットで見たんだけど、高級官僚が役所を退職したあと天下りで公社や公団を渡りあるいて退職金を稼ぐのも渡り鳥なんて揶揄されるから、一概にいいイメージではなくてね」
lines.english: “Ah, but Miss *Making It Through a World Full of Demons*, I read online that *migratory bird* is also a sneer for senior bureaucrats who retire, descend from heaven into one public corporation after another, and collect a retirement payout at every stop. So it doesn't have an entirely positive image.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　だったら如実にこいつの腹黒さを表してンじゃねえか。うぉんむ、うぉんむ。これはしたり、ぶもははは」
lines.english: “Huh? Then it expresses her black-hearted scheming perfectly. Hrrm, hrrm. How very apt. Bmohahaha!”

lines.japanese: 「ねー、せめてもう少し女の子らしい扱いしてくれてもよくない？」
lines.english: “Hey, couldn't you treat me at least a little more like a girl?”

lines.japanese: 「るふう、なりたなりたと姦しいわっぱめ。そう申すならば、おなごらしく喘ぎ声のひとつもあげてみせよ」
lines.english: “Rrgh. Cross this, cross that—what a clamorous little brat. If thou demandest treatment as a woman, then let us hear thee produce one womanly moan.”

lines.japanese: 「あげたことないから分からないよね」
lines.english: “I've never made one, so I wouldn't know how.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだ渡りに船さん、その程度もあげたことないのか。ちなみに俺は、生まれて初めて発した声が『お兄ちゃん、そっちの穴はらめえ』だぞ」
lines.english: “What is this, Miss Boat at the Crossing? You have never even managed that? Why, the first words I uttered upon entering this world were, ‘Big Brother, not that hole!’”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君がいたら淫行三昧の日々を送って、毎日喘いでる予定だったんだよね」
lines.english: “If Haneda were here, I was planning a daily life of nonstop debauchery and constant moaning.”
“Seriously!?”

lines.japanese: 「だって私、羽田君の恋人だもん」
lines.english: “Because I'm Haneda's girlfriend.”

lines.japanese: 「う、ううう、うるさい！　仮面恋人のくせに、心にもないこと言うなっ！　ほほほほんのちょっぴりドキッとしちゃったじゃねえか、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ。ウヴァーフシュ、ウヴァーフシュ」
lines.english: “S-s-silence! You're only his pretend girlfriend, so don't say things you don't mean! Y-you made my heart jump the tiniest bit. I'll fucking kill you, asshole. Uvah-fsh! Uvah-fsh!”

lines.japanese: ぐぬぬ……女狐めが、勝ちほこった笑みを……！
lines.english: Ngh... That vixen, smiling in triumph...!

lines.japanese: 「ふ、ふーんだ！　冗談じゃないですよー、貴様なんか頼まれたって愛人一号にもしてやらないよーんだ」
lines.english: “H-hmph! As if! Even if you begged, I wouldn't make you Mistress Number One!”

lines.japanese: 「愛人……？　ってことは、もしかしてぱね田くんには、本命の好きなひとがいるの？」
lines.english: “Mistress...? Wait, Paneda, is there somebody you're actually in love with?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「……いませんヨ？」
lines.english: “...Nooo?”

lines.japanese: 「今の間はなに」
lines.english: “What was that pause?”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、ホントいないいない」
lines.english: “No, no. I really don't.”

lines.japanese: 「なになに、教えてよ。相談に乗ったげるからさ」
lines.english: “What? Tell me! I'll give you advice.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　んだテメ、その愉快そうな顔は。１２０％冷やかしのツラじゃねえか、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Huh? What's with that delighted face? That's a face poised to tease me at one hundred and twenty percent output. I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「真面目だって。ホント誰にも言わないよ、約束するぷくく」
lines.english: “I'm serious. I really won't tell anybody. I promise. Pffft.”

lines.japanese: 「アレッ！？　いまなんか漏れましたよねえ！？」
lines.english: “Huh!? Something leaked out just now, didn't it!?”

lines.japanese: 「ねえねえ、このクラスの子？　ていうか学校のひと？ 教えてよぱね山くん」
lines.english: “Come on. Is she in this class? Is she even at this school? Tell me, Paneyama.”

lines.japanese: 「さりげなく名前変えるな。言わないって言ってるだろう」
lines.english: “Don't casually change my name. I said I won't tell you.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ！　言わないってことは好きなひといるんだ！」
lines.english: “Ah! If you won't tell me, that means there *is* somebody!”

lines.japanese: 「問うに落ちず、語るに落ちた！？」
lines.english: “I resisted the questions, then gave myself away talking?!”

lines.japanese: 「ふ～ん、好きなひといるんだあ。いいねえ、青春だねえ、毎日が薔薇色だねえ」
lines.english: “Hmm. So there is someone you like. How lovely. Youth! Every day rose-colored!”

lines.japanese: くっ、水を得た魚のように……やっぱりこの女はＳだ。
lines.english: Ngh. Like a fish returned to water... This woman truly was a sadist.

lines.japanese: 「う、うるさい。べつに恋愛感情とかそういうんじゃないんだ。ちょっと、その、わけがあって……大事な存在っていうか、まあ、特別な相手っていうだけだ」
lines.english: “Sh-shut up. It isn't romantic love or anything like that. There are... circumstances. She's an important presence, I suppose. Someone special. That's all.”

lines.japanese: ……だよね？
lines.english: ...Right?

lines.japanese: し、信じてない。あの目は明らかに信じてない。ああくそ、もういやだ、やっぱりこいつは危険だ。
lines.english: She did not believe me. Those eyes plainly did not believe me. Damn it. I'd had enough. This woman really was dangerous.

lines.japanese: 「ほ、本日の会議はここまで！　非協力的な班員が一名いたため作業は進まず、と担任には報告しておく！」
lines.english: “T-that's all for today's meeting! I shall report to our homeroom teacher that no work was completed due to one uncooperative group member!”

lines.japanese: 「一名っていうか、全班員やる気ないよね」
lines.english: “One? Every member of this group is unmotivated.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、まあ……だな。むしろ俺と渡来明日香は、こうして放課後に集まってる分だけ他二名よりは──」
lines.english: “Well... yes. If anything, the fact that Asuka Watarai and I gather here after school means we're doing more than the other two—”

lines.japanese: 「──あ、そうだ。朝、学校くる途中で俺、山科京に会ってさ」
lines.english: “—oh, right. I saw Miyako Yamashina on the way to school this morning.”

lines.japanese: 「え、山科？」
lines.english: “What? Yamashina?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、病状が快復したら、こっち手伝ってくれって頼んどいた。快く承諾してくれたぞ」
lines.english: “Yes. I asked her to help once her condition improves. She gladly agreed.”

lines.japanese: 「というわけだから、渡来明日香は針生蔵人を勧誘しておいてくれ」
lines.english: “Therefore, Asuka Watarai, you shall recruit Kurodo Hariu.”

lines.japanese: 「私が？　なんで？」
lines.english: “Me? Why?”

lines.japanese: 「俺はひとりスカウトしたんだから、次は当然おまえの番だろう」
lines.english: “I scouted one person, so obviously it's your turn next.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん……まあ、もっともっちゃー、もっともだけど……」
lines.english: “Hmm... Well, I suppose that's fair enough...”

lines.japanese: 「よし、任せたぞ！　さあ、いよいよ本格的始動の日も近いな。ははは、どうだ渡来明日香、胸がおどるだろう！」
lines.english: “Good. I'm counting on you! The day of our true beginning is nearly here. Ha ha ha! Tell me, Asuka Watarai—does your heart not dance?”

lines.japanese: 会議も踊る、されどちょっと進んだ。
lines.english: The meeting danced, but it did make a little progress.

lines.japanese: と思う。
lines.english: I think.

lines.japanese: さて、テンションが上向きのうちに。
lines.english: Now, while my spirits were still rising.

lines.japanese: この前は失敗したが、今日こそ親友の森里君と電話でお話をしちゃうぞ。
lines.english: I messed it up last time, but today I was finally gonna talk on the phone with my dear friend Morisato.

lines.japanese: マナーを守る紳士の森里君だから、きっと病室にいるうちはケータイの電源を切っているだろう。
lines.english: As a gentleman attentive to manners, Morisato would surely keep his phone switched off while inside the hospital room.

lines.japanese: でも前回と同じぐらいの時間だから、いまならまた屋上にいるかもしれない。俺は高鳴る胸を押さえながら彼の番号を呼びだした。
lines.english: But it was about the same time as my previous call. Perhaps he was on the roof again. Pressing a hand to my pounding heart, I called his number.

lines.japanese: ぷっ　ぷっ　ぷっ　ぷっ……。
lines.english: Beep... beep... beep... beep...

lines.japanese: ぷるるるる、ぷるるるる……ブッ！
lines.english: Brrring, brrring... Click!

lines.japanese: 「だれ」
lines.english: “Who is this?”
“Mor!”

lines.japanese: 「もっ、もももも森っ、もり、もりもり森里君！？　おれっ、俺だよ俺ヨージだよ！」
lines.english: “M-M-M-Mori—Mori, Mori, Morisato!? It's me! It's Yoji!”

lines.japanese: 俺は胸の高ぶりを抑えきれなかった。
lines.english: I couldn't contain my excitement.

lines.japanese: 「うぉーい、カンベンしてよ、またイタ電かよ」
lines.english: “Oh, come on. Give me a break. Another prank call?”

lines.japanese: 「ま、まま、待ってよもりもり森里君！　あのね今日はねすごくね、すごく大事な話があるんだ。ちゃんと聞いてよマジてめブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ、あのね実はね本当はね、本当は俺ヨージじゃなくて──」
lines.english: “W-w-wait, Mori-Mori-Morisato! Listen, I have something really, really important to tell you today. Listen properly, damn it, or I'll fucking kill you, asshole. See, the truth is, I'm not really Yoji—”

lines.japanese: 「ああワリ、俺いま看護師のお姉さんと話してッとこだから。切るわ」
lines.english: “Ah, sorry. I'm in the middle of talking to this nurse, so I'm hanging up.”

lines.japanese: プツッ！
lines.english: Click!

lines.japanese: ああ……切られてしまった……。
lines.english: Ah... He had hung up...

lines.japanese: 歯がゆいな。まるで運命が俺たちふたりを引きさいてるみたいだ。
lines.english: How frustrating. It was as though fate itself were tearing the two of us apart.

lines.japanese: うん、だけど森里君はナース好きだということが分かったぞ。ようし、それなら次は対策を立ててから電話してみよう。
lines.english: Still, I had learned that Morisato liked nurses. Good. Next time, I would devise a countermeasure before I called.

lines.japanese: きっと彼だって、俺が親友の羽田タカシだってことに気付けば、たちまち話をしたくなるはず。そう、それだ。だから待っててね森里君。
lines.english: The moment he realized I was his dear friend Takashi Haneda, he was bound to want to talk. Yes. That was it. So wait for me, Morisato.
